question: Will Judge McCaslin order the State to produce additional discovery at the October 16, 2026 Murdaugh retrial hearing?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: defense motions to compel discovery in high-profile homicide cases are fairly often granted in part (~50-60%), and any partial grant of any of four categories counts here. Judge McCaslin called an urgent in-person hearing after defense letters showed the State was unresponsive; at Aug 14 she ruled from the bench granting partial relief (limited quantitative DNA testing, in-camera review of agents' files). Raw FARO scan files and phone extraction files are low-cost, standard discovery items likely ordered. Risks for NO: postponement, matters taken under advisement with written order after Oct 16, the DNA question deferred to a follow-up profiling hearing, or the State voluntarily agreeing so that no 'order' is reported. No prediction market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold.
calls.dossier:
- Oct 2, 2026 (WRDW/WTOC): Judge Debra McCaslin set an in-person hearing at 10 a.m. Oct 16 at the Lexington courthouse on 'urgent evidentiary' issues: DNA, cellphone extraction files, ballistic data, and FARO scan data. The State's response is due at noon Oct 8. All other motions go to Nov 13.
- Oct 1, 2026 (WRDW): Harpootlian's letter to the judge says the defense sent 4 letters (Sept 11, 15, 21, 30) and filed 3 motions to compel but got only one State response (Sept 17).
- Sept 18 motion (ABC News 4, FITSNews Sept 18/22): asks for further/Y-STR testing of Maggie's fingernail DNA and her phone swabs at Othram; SLED records on .300 Blackout ammunition (720 cartridge cases entered in SLED's database since Jan 2021); native FARO scan data (the defense got only a read-only viewer in 2022; the kennel has since been demolished). It asks for production within 10 days.
- Sept 17 letter from Creighton Waters (FITSNews Sept 22): calls the male DNA 'extremely low' and says more testing could consume the remaining material; says no SLED database link to other shootings; opposes releasing cartridge cases from open Allendale County investigations. The State did not concede production.
- Sept 28 motion: compel cellphone extraction files. Sept 30 motion: compel evidence about alleged disposal of the murder weapons / police cover-up claims (Post and Courier, FITSNews).
- Aug 2026 hearing (Newsweek; Yahoo): McCaslin ruled from the bench on several items: venue moved out of the 14th Circuit, she took control of jury summons, she will do an in-camera review of SLED agents' personnel files for Brady/Giglio. She allowed DNA material to be sent for an initial quantity measurement only, with results reported back before any further testing.
- Status quo: no production order yet on these categories; the State's position is that discovery obligations have been met.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off media reports (FITSNews, ABC News 4) of an order at or in connection with the Oct 16 hearing compelling production or testing; under-advisement rulings, briefing orders, or scheduling a DNA profiling hearing alone count as NO; a postponement means NO.

calls.reconciliation: No web access on this run. The factual disputes between the dossiers (whether venue was decided Aug 14 or later; the exact count and dates of defense letters, 4 vs 5; Othram's Y-target detail) do not bear on the outcome and could not be settled from the dossiers; they carry no weight. All three runs agree on the decisive facts: the judge set an urgent hearing on DNA, phone extractions, ballistics and FARO; the State's response is due Oct 8; the State has largely not responded; the judge ruled from the bench on Aug 14 but staged the DNA testing. The remaining dispute is judgment: how much weight to give mooting, staging and under-advisement versus the judge's demonstrated willingness to grant partial relief from the bench. I weight the low-cost raw-data categories (FARO, phone extractions) as the most likely grant, and I count a judge memorializing State agreement as an order as likely to be reported as YES. I land at 0.61.
